subject: astronomy
title: Coordinates Calculations
welcome_lead: Convert between horizontal and equatorial coordinate systems.
meta_desc: GCSE Astronomy calculations: RA, declination, altitude and azimuth.
final_note: Coordinates make the sky a precise grid you can navigate.

concepts.def: Angle of object above horizon (0 to 90 degrees).
Angle along horizon measured clockwise from north.
Angular distance west of the local meridian.
Imaginary circle through zenith and celestial poles.

walkthroughs.body_html: Altitude: 0 degrees at horizon, 90 degrees at zenith. Azimuth: 0 degrees north, 90 degrees east, 180 degrees south, 270 degrees west. These change as the sky rotates.
RA is measured in hours, minutes and seconds eastwards along the celestial equator from the vernal equinox. Dec is measured in degrees north (+) or south (-) of the celestial equator.
The altitude of Polaris in the sky equals your latitude. From London (~51.5 N), Polaris sits ~51.5 degrees above the northern horizon.
